transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, hi. Well... I guess I've just been having some trouble at work lately. I keep losing my place when I'm trying to schedule appointments, or... when I'm working on the lobby displays. 

My mind just sort of slips off track. I get caught up thinking about things I might have overlooked, and... yeah. That's mainly why I came in.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy lately?
Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think so. I still do the things I usually do. I'm just... having trouble focusing at work, like I said.
Have you noticed yourself feeling more irritable, or maybe not getting as much pleasure out of things as you used to?
Um... no. I don't think I'm irritable. And... I still enjoy my usual things fine. It's really just... what I mentioned before.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy lately?
Um... I think you just asked me that. Like I said... no. I'm not feeling down or hopeless. It's really just the distraction at work.
Have you had any trouble concentrating on tasks, even outside of work, like following conversations or reading?

Well... mostly it's just at work. That's really what made me come in. I just keep losing my place when I'm scheduling appointments, or... working on the lobby displays. My mind just kind of slips off track, I guess, because I'm busy thinking about what I might have overlooked.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?
No... I really haven't. I feel like you keep asking me about being sad or hopeless, but... no. I haven't had anything like that. It's just the stuff at work I mentioned.
Would you say you’ve had little interest or pleasure in doing things lately, even the ones you usually enjoy?
Um... no. Not really. I still like doing my normal things. It's just... like I said, it's really just the work stuff. I don't know why we keep going over this part.
Have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than a couple of days in a row, even if it wasn’t recent?
No... I really haven't. I don't... I don't know how else to tell you this. I just don't get down like that. It's never been an issue for me, not even in the past.
Have you ever felt down or sad for a couple of days in a row, even if it didn't last very long or seem serious?
No. I... I really haven't. I don't know what else to say about it. Just... no.
Have you ever, even for a short time, felt a change in your mood or enjoyment of things, even if it didn’t last long or seemed minor?
I mean... I feel like I keep answering the same thing. No. I haven't noticed anything like that. My mood is fine.
Have you ever had a time when you didn't care about things that usually matter to you, even if it didn't last very long?
I... no. Like I just said, my mood is fine. I still care about the things I usually do. I haven't had that happen.
Can you describe your mood during the times when you're struggling with focus at work? Does it affect how you feel emotionally, or do you feel the same as always?
I don't know... I guess I just feel the same as always. I'm just at my desk trying to get things done. It doesn't really change how I feel emotionally. I just have a hard time focusing, that's all.
Do you often feel worried or anxious about things, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

I guess... yeah. Just about ordinary things, though. Like the schedules at work, or bills... travel plans. Sometimes just little paperwork errors. I just... I start thinking that one small mix-up is going to turn into a much bigger problem. But it's just regular stuff.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or on edge most days, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?

I suppose so. I mean... I'm at the front desk all day, so I have to keep smiling and helping people, but... I don't know. Inside, I just feel wound really tight. Like my shoulders are always up around my ears, and I'm just... waiting for something to go wrong. It's most days, I guess.
Do you find it hard to stop worrying once you start, even about things that might seem small or unlikely?

Um... yeah, I suppose. It's... it's hard to just turn it off. I can tell myself, like... 'Sunny, it's handled.' But the thought just keeps looping anyway. And... I don't know, pretty soon I've gone from that one concern to another, and I'm just... checking all the details in my head over and over.
Do you notice any physical signs like restlessness, feeling fatigued, or muscle tension when you're feeling anxious?
I don't really know. I guess I'm just... tired a lot. And like I said, my shoulders are usually pretty tight. But I don't really notice anything else.
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried on most days, even when there isn’t a specific problem happening at the time?

I guess... yeah, like I said before. It's most days. And it's not usually some big emergency, just... ordinary things. Work schedules, the bills... travel plans. Even just a little paperwork error at the desk. I don't know, it just feels like one small mix-up is going to turn into some much bigger problem. So I just... worry about it.
Would you say that your worry or anxiety has been difficult to control and has been causing you significant distress or affecting your daily life, even outside of work?

I mean... I'm still showing up and getting through the day. It's not like I can't function. It's just... scheduling takes me a lot longer now, I guess. I end up double-checking myself so much. And... I don't know, I've had to redo parts of the lobby displays a few times recently, just from losing track of what I was arranging. So... yeah, I suppose it affects things a little.
